steps.title: Mark the parts and check the stock
steps.text: Check that the plywood is flat and the tread panels are sound, then mark both side-support outlines from the dimensions in the plan. Mark the two tread blanks at 464 × 300mm. Label the inside faces of P1 and P2 so the matching sides stay oriented correctly.
steps.tip: Measure from one square reference edge and mark waste clearly before cutting.

steps.title: Cut the side supports
steps.text: Cut P1 and P2 to 500 × 425mm blanks, then cut the stair-step profile: the low ledge is 200mm high through z=300mm, and the upper ledge is 425mm high from z=300 to 500mm. Keep the matching profiles identical and sand any small irregularities smooth.
tools_used: Circular saw with guide or track saw
steps.safety: Wear eye, hearing, and dust protection. Clamp the plywood securely, keep hands clear of the blade, and support the offcut so it cannot pinch the saw.
steps.tip: Make a full-size template to confirm both supports match before sanding.

steps.title: Cut and ease the treads
steps.text: Cut P3 and P4 to 464 × 300 × 25mm. Ease the exposed corners and edges lightly, then sand the tread faces smooth. Keep the upper and lower treads clearly labeled.
tools_used: Circular saw with guide or track saw
steps.safety: Wear eye, hearing, and dust protection while cutting and sanding. Clamp the stock and keep hands clear of the cutting path.
steps.tip: Do not round the mating ends so much that the treads no longer sit flat on their supports.

steps.title: Prepare the cleats and brace holes
steps.text: Buy and cut two 19 × 38 × 220mm hardwood cleats for P3 and two 19 × 38 × 180mm cleats for P4. In each cleat, mark three 6mm bolt holes along its length, at least 30mm from the ends; also make one round retainer hole at the depth midpoint and two 14 × 7mm slots oriented front-to-back. Check the X-brace strap layout against the inside faces of P1 and P2, then drill its bolt holes before assembly.
steps.safety: Clamp all small stock securely before drilling and wear eye protection. Keep hands clear of the bit and use a depth stop to avoid drilling through the tread's visible face.
steps.tip: Do not make retainer slots wider than needed; the washers must fully cover them throughout their travel.

steps.title: Sand and prepare for finish
steps.text: Sand the plywood faces and cut edges, removing splinters and sharp corners. Sand the tread faces progressively through 120 and 180 grit. Keep the cleat-to-plywood contact areas bare so the cleats seat flat.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection; vacuum dust rather than blowing it into the air.
steps.tip: Keep the tread support surfaces flat; heavy rounding can reduce bearing contact.

steps.title: Finish the parts and install the X-brace
steps.text: Paint P1 and P2 dark, leaving the cleat contact areas bare. Apply clear finish to P3 and P4 and allow it to cure before assembly. Before the treads go on, fit the two steel straps as an X between P1 and P2 beneath the upper tread; use four M6 × 35mm through-bolts at the strap ends and one at the crossing, with washers and nyloc nuts, and tighten securely.
steps.safety: Work with ventilation, wear gloves when handling finishes, and keep finishes away from flames. Wear eye protection while drilling or tightening hardware; support the side panels so they cannot tip.
steps.tip: Dry-fit the X-brace and verify it clears both treads and all cleats before tightening its bolts.

steps.title: Bolt on the bearing cleats and retain the treads
steps.text: Position each cleat on the inside face of its side support, with the top flush to the tread underside. For each cleat, install three M6 × 70mm through-bolts with washers and nyloc nuts; snug the nuts without crushing the plywood. Set P3 on its two lower cleats and P4 on its two upper cleats, then drive three 38mm #8 screws with washers upward through each cleat into each tread: use the midpoint round hole as the fixed reference and the two front-to-back slots as sliding retainers. Do not glue the treads to the cleats; check that each tread is level and the side supports remain parallel.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while drilling and tightening. Keep the stool supported and stable, and do not place body weight on it during assembly.
steps.tip: Confirm the washers cover the slots and that the screws can slide slightly along the slots before final tightening.

steps.title: Inspect and add mandatory tread traction
steps.text: After the glue-free assembly and all finishes have fully cured, check every bolt and screw, confirm the stool sits without rocking on a level floor, and inspect for cracks or loose joints. Apply walking-surface-rated anti-slip strips across the normal foot-contact area on both treads, including near each leading edge; follow the tape maker's cleaning and bonding instructions and press the adhesive down firmly. Do not leave the front landing area unprotected.
steps.safety: Do not climb on the stool during assembly or while finishes or anti-slip adhesive are curing. Use it only on a flat, dry surface; stop using it if it rocks, loosens, or shows damage.
steps.tip: Use only anti-slip material rated for walking surfaces and replace it if it lifts, wears smooth, or becomes contaminated.

Use paints and finishes with good ventilation, follow their labels, and allow the stated cure time before use.
Use only on a flat, dry floor. This DIY stool is not a ladder and has no tested or certified load rating; inspect it before each use.

parts.name: Chair rear legs and back uprights
parts.notes: Continuous vertical rear posts. Seat-support and lower side rails join into their front-facing ends.

parts.name: Chair side seat rails
parts.notes: Run front-to-back between the front legs and rear posts; tenons at each end are not shown in the bounding-box placement.

parts.name: Chair front and rear seat rails

parts.name: Chair seat

parts.name: Chair backrest
parts.notes: Flat, rounded backrest; its rear face meets the front faces of the rear posts.

parts.name: Chair lower side stretchers

parts.name: Chair lower cross stretcher

joints.drive_from: From pocket holes in the inside face of each P3 apron end, before the desktop is fitted; screws enter leg side grain.
joints.note: Use the pocket-jig manufacturer's setting for 19 mm stock, coarse-thread screws, and glue on the contact faces. Verify the setup on matching offcuts.

joints.drive_from: From pocket holes on the inside face of each P2 end into the face of P3; assemble before the desktop is fitted.
joints.note: Glue the contacting apron faces. Use a jig setting for 19 mm material and test on offcuts.

joints.drive_from: Bearing contact only at the leg tops; no screw is driven into leg end grain.
joints.note: The desktop rests on the legs and is fastened to the aprons.

joints.drive_from: From the desktop top face through countersunk pilot holes into each P2 apron.
joints.note: Plywood top; no glue is needed. The screws pass through 18 mm plywood and engage 20 mm of the apron.

joints.drive_from: From the desktop top face through countersunk pilot holes into each P3 apron, centered across its 19 mm thickness.
joints.note: Plywood top; no glue is needed. Ensure each pilot hole is centered on the narrow apron top.

joints.drive_from: Fit and clamp the shouldered rail tenons into mortises in the rear-facing sides of the front legs before attaching the seat.
joints.note: Use glued, shouldered tenons approximately 10 mm thick x 25 mm wide x 20 mm long; shoulders bear against the legs. This is a structural chair joint.

joints.drive_from: Fit and clamp the shouldered rail tenons into mortises in the front-facing sides of the rear posts before attaching the seat.
joints.note: Use glued, shouldered tenons approximately 10 mm thick x 25 mm wide x 20 mm long; shoulders bear against the posts. This resists leverage from the backrest.

joints.drive_from: Fit cross-rail tenons into mortises in the inner faces of P7 before the seat is attached.
joints.note: Use glued, shouldered tenons approximately 10 mm thick x 25 mm wide x 20 mm long. The four joints connect front and rear rails to both side rails.

joints.drive_from: Fit the front ends of the lower side-stretcher tenons into mortises in the rear-facing sides of P5 before the chair frame is closed.
joints.note: Use glued, shouldered tenons approximately 10 mm thick x 25 mm wide x 20 mm long.

joints.drive_from: Fit the rear ends of the lower side-stretcher tenons into mortises in the front-facing sides of P6 before the chair frame is closed.
joints.note: Use glued, shouldered tenons approximately 10 mm thick x 25 mm wide x 20 mm long.

joints.drive_from: Fit the cross-stretcher tenons into mortises in the inner faces of the lower side stretchers before the frame is closed.
joints.note: Use glued, shouldered tenons approximately 10 mm thick x 25 mm wide x 20 mm long. This cross stretcher braces the frame across its width.

joints.drive_from: From the top of the seat through countersunk pilot holes into each side rail.
joints.note: No glue; the seat is replaceable. Screws pass through 18 mm plywood and engage about 20 mm of rail.

joints.drive_from: From the top of the seat through countersunk pilot holes into the front and rear cross rails.
joints.note: No glue; the seat is replaceable. Keep pilot holes centered on each rail.

joints.drive_from: Bearing contact only: the seat rests on the tops of the front legs; do not fasten into leg end grain.
joints.note: The seat is secured to the support rails by J12 and J13; this contact is supplemental bearing support.

joints.drive_from: Edge contact only at the rear seat edge and post fronts; the seat is secured to the frame by J12 and J13.
joints.note: No fastener is driven through the seat edge.

joints.drive_from: From the front face of the backrest through countersunk pilot holes into each rear post.
joints.note: No glue; the panel is replaceable. Screws pass through 18 mm plywood and engage about 20 mm of post side grain.

tools.name: Circular saw with straightedge guide
tools.alternative: Have the store make straight cuts or use a handsaw with a guide.

tools.name: Drill/driver with countersink bit
tools.alternative: Use a hand drill and manual countersink; allow extra time.

steps.title: Cut the frame stock and panels
steps.text: Cut P1–P3 and P5–P8 and P11–P12 to their listed lengths. Cut P4, P9, and P10 from 18 mm plywood, or have the store cut rectangular blanks. Check each part with a square and label it.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection; secure stock before cutting and keep hands clear of the blade.
steps.tip: Cut matching parts as a pair and compare their lengths before moving on.

steps.title: Shape panels and prepare chair joinery
steps.text: Round the corners of P4, P9, and P10 and ease sharp edges. Lay out the mortises and matching tenons for P7, P8, P11, and P12; cut them to the dimensions in the joint notes and test each fit on offcuts first. Sand all parts before assembly.
tools_used: Router with straight bit and edge guide
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and a dust mask; clamp parts securely and keep hands clear of router bits and chisels.
steps.tip: Leave tenons slightly proud and pare them to a snug fit; do not force a tight tenon into a thin leg.

steps.title: Drill desk apron pocket holes
steps.text: Set the pocket-hole jig and stop collar for 19 mm stock. Drill two holes at each end of P2 and P3, on their inside faces. Dry-fit the desk apron arrangement before gluing.
tools_used: Pocket-hole jig with 19 mm setting and stop collar
steps.safety: Clamp each apron securely before drilling and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Test the jig setting and screw length on matching 19 mm offcuts to prevent breakthrough.

steps.title: Assemble the desk leg-and-apron frame
steps.text: Join the two P3 side aprons to the P1 legs with two 32 mm coarse-thread pocket screws at each end, driving from the apron inside faces into leg side grain. Join P2 to P3 with two 32 mm coarse-thread pocket screws at each apron end, driving from P2 into the P3 faces. Apply glue at each contact, clamp the frame square, and let the glue cure as directed.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while driving screws and keep fingers clear of clamps.
steps.tip: Measure both frame diagonals; equal measurements indicate the frame is square.

steps.title: Attach the desktop
steps.text: Set P4 on the desk frame with an even overhang. Drive three 38 mm screws through P4 into each P2 apron and two centered screws into each P3 apron; do not drive screws into leg end grain. No glue is needed at the plywood top joint.
steps.safety: Support the desktop while positioning it and wear eye protection when drilling.
steps.tip: Pre-drill and countersink from the top; confirm on an offcut that screws cannot break through the aprons.

steps.title: Assemble the chair frame and lower stretchers
steps.text: Glue and clamp the shouldered mortise-and-tenon joints for P7 into P5 and P6, then fit P8 between the side rails. Fit and glue P11 between the front legs and rear posts, and P12 between the lower side stretchers. Clamp the complete frame square and level, and allow the glue to cure fully before adding panels.
tools_used: Router with straight bit and edge guide
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and secure the frame before using chisels or a router; get help to handle the frame if needed.
steps.tip: The tenon shoulders should seat firmly against the post faces; do not use screws to compensate for a loose mortise-and-tenon fit.

steps.title: Fasten the chair seat
steps.text: Center P9 on the chair frame. Pre-drill and countersink two holes above each P7 and P8 rail, then drive 38 mm screws from the seat top into the rails. Do not glue the seat; its bearing on the front-leg tops is supplemental, not the main connection.
steps.safety: Support or clamp the seat while drilling and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Mark rail centerlines on masking tape so every screw enters solid wood.

steps.title: Attach the backrest
steps.text: Position P10 against the front faces of P6 with its lower edge at the listed height. Drive two 38 mm screws through countersunk pilot holes into each rear post. Do not glue the backrest so it can be replaced.
steps.safety: Support and clamp the backrest before drilling; wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Measure from the seat to both ends of the backrest to keep it level.

steps.title: Paint the frames
steps.text: Mask the plywood panels as needed and apply black enamel to the desk and chair frames. Follow the paint label for recoat and cure times. Keep wet finish out of screw recesses that may need service.
steps.safety: Work with good ventilation, protect skin and eyes, and follow the paint label; keep wet finishes away from flames and children.
steps.tip: Use thin coats to avoid runs at inside corners.

steps.title: Finish the desktop, seat, and backrest
steps.text: Apply a dark wood-look finish to P4 and orange paint to P9 and P10. Seal exposed plywood edges and allow each coat to dry fully according to the product label before use.
steps.safety: Use ventilation and gloves as directed on the finish label; keep solvent-based products away from ignition sources.
steps.tip: Test the desktop finish on an offcut first because plywood veneer can absorb stain unevenly.

steps.title: Inspect the finished set
steps.text: Check that the desk frame is square and does not wobble. Inspect the chair mortise-and-tenon shoulders, stretchers, seat screws, and backrest screws; do not use the chair if any joint moves, cracks, or has a visible gap. Retighten serviceable screws periodically.
steps.safety: Do not stand on the desk or chair. Test the chair by sitting normally on a level floor, and stop using it if a joint shifts or the frame cracks.
steps.tip: Reinspect the chair after its first few uses and periodically afterward.

safety_overview: Wear safety glasses for cutting, routing, chiseling, drilling, and fastening; add hearing protection for powered tools.
Use a dust mask while cutting or sanding plywood and timber; ventilate well when painting or applying finish.
Clamp work securely, keep hands clear of blades and bits, and unplug tools before changing blades or bits.
Support large panels during cuts and lifting; keep the desk and chair on a level floor and never stand or climb on them.
Let finishes cure as directed before use, and inspect chair joints and fasteners regularly.

review.summary: The desk assembly sequence is generally workable, but its apron stock specification and pocket-screw selection conflict. The chair needs stronger leg-to-rail joinery and racking resistance before it is suitable for normal sitting loads.

issues.problem: J6 and J7 make the chair's primary leg-to-seat-frame connections with pocket screws and glued rail ends. These joints must withstand repeated sideways loads and leverage from the tall back posts. Gluing the rail ends does not provide dependable reinforcement, and there are no lower stretchers or other dedicated racking braces. The screwed-on seat does not adequately protect the leg joints from these loads.
issues.fix: Replace J6 and J7 with properly specified structural chair joints, such as mortise-and-tenon joints with shoulders bearing against the posts. Add lower side stretchers and a cross stretcher with structural joinery to resist racking in both directions. Update the parts, tools, joint details, and step 6 before retaining the adult/student seating claim; do not treat the gradual load test as a substitute for adequate joinery.

issues.problem: Step 3 specifies a pocket-hole jig setting for 19 mm stock, but J1 and J2 specify 50 mm pocket screws. That is not the normal screw length for this stock thickness and can cause breakthrough or splitting rather than a reliable apron connection.
issues.fix: If P2 and P3 remain 19 mm thick, replace the 50 mm screws in J1, J2, and step 4 with the jig manufacturer's specified screws for 19 mm softwood stock, typically approximately 32 mm coarse-thread pocket screws. Set both the jig and drill stop accordingly and verify the connection on matching offcuts.

issues.problem: P2 and P3 are specified as actual 19 x 60 mm stock, but their notes describe a 38 mm frame thickness. Rotating a 19 x 60 mm board cannot produce a 38 mm thickness. The builder cannot tell which stock and joint setup the author intends.
issues.fix: Choose one actual apron cross-section and use it consistently in the material specifications, part notes, illustrations, and drilling instructions. If retaining 19 x 60 mm stock, remove the statements describing it as 38 mm thick and use pocket-hole settings and hardware appropriate to 19 mm material.

issues.problem: Step 6 proceeds from dry-fitting directly to glue and screws without explicitly instructing the builder to drill the chair pocket holes first. Unlike step 3 for the desk, it gives no jig setup or drilling sequence for these thicker rails.
issues.fix: After revising the chair structure, explicitly instruct the builder to drill any retained pocket holes while the rails are separate and before applying glue. For J8, specify the jig and stop settings for the actual 38 mm stock, confirm screw length with the jig manufacturer, and assemble with the underside pockets accessible before fitting P9.

issues.problem: The instruction to use a dark stain 'or' clear coat allows stain alone to be treated as the finished desktop surface. Ordinary wood stain provides color, not adequate protection against classroom spills and wear.
issues.fix: For unfinished plywood, specify optional stain followed by a compatible durable clear furniture finish, including the edges and underside. For a pre-laminated top, omit stain and follow the laminate supplier's edge-sealing instructions.
